thread:
infra-bot: ALERT: hosted-api queue length in us-west-2 exceeded threshold (3000) — severity: high. Auto-remediation attempted: scale-up request created to provisioner, status=FAILED (quota_error).

jordan.t: seeing huge p95/p99 spikes across text-generation routes. Customers report timeouts. p95 ~ 1.8s -> 6.2s, p99 hitting 24s and timing out. Queue length trending up: 1800 -> 4200 in 12m.

sre-oncall: ack — grabbing logs and provisioning status. Opening incident channel.

sre-oncall: quick TL;DR: autoscaler API call to provision GPUs returned 429 from cloud (quota), provisioner retried -> backoff -> no new nodes. We are backlogged; eviction/placement latencies increased.

jordan.t: logs snippet from provisioner: 
```
2026-03-15T03:10:12Z provisioner.go:requestNodePoolProvision error=QuotaExceeded: Insufficient GPU quota for region us-west-2
status_code=429 request_id=abc-123
```

maria.k: can we route traffic to dedicated pools / smaller-quantized model variants to relieve load? Also consider enabling prefix-KV cache bypass to speed small queries.

kyra: on standby to run fallback routing. I can flip routing rule to send non-SLA customers to fallback-quantized v1 (half-precision) and preserve capacity for enterprise tenants. Needs a small config change in routing svc.

sre-oncall: doing that now. Command: 
```bash
# enable routing rule to fallback pool
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" 
  https://ops-api.internal/routing/rules 
  -d '{"match": "tier!=enterprise", "route_to": "fallback-quantized-v1", "priority": 900}'
```

sre-oncall: applied rule. Confirmed ~40% of requests for non-enterprise have fallen off the hosted queue and are hitting fallback pool. Queue growth rate slowed.

jordan.t: nice, raw numbers: backlog peak 4200 -> 2600 in 8m after routing flip. p95 down to 3.1s, p99 still high 14s. We need additional mitigations.

maria.k: can we also enable request shedding for very large token requests (>2k tokens) to keep latency SLOs? Maybe respond with 429 + Retry-After for best-effort customers.

sre-oncall: enabling token-size-based throttle on the gateway. Patch applying: 
```json
{"throttle": {"max_input_tokens": 2000, "action": "reject", "status": 429}}
```

sre-oncall: throttle live. Early telemetry: ~2.5% of incoming requests are being shed. Helps tail latencies.

kyra: reaching out to cloud quota team now — filed emergency quota request (ticket# 78910) for +30 GPU quota in us-west-2. ETA unknown. If approved we can scale the pools automatically.

support-bot: Auto-message to downstream support channels: "Investigating elevated latencies/timeouts for hosted API in us-west-2. Some customers may see degraded performance. We will provide updates every 15 minutes." :warning:

eng-lead: what's the customer impact? Any high-spend customers affected? Need list to notify CSMs.

jordan.t: enterprise tenants pinned to dedicated pools are unaffected. A subset of high-RTU customers not pinned were routed to fallback after the rule, so they may see lower quality but reduced latency. Unpinned high-volume customers (approx 12 accounts) saw 5-15% increased error rates during the spike window.

maria.k: recommendation: increase fallback pool capacity (use smaller instance types but more of them) and resume gradual routing back once queue under 1000. Also schedule an offline job to requeue long-running requests when the backlog clears.

sre-oncall: provisioner still returning quota errors for large node shapes, but small GPU shapes can be created — attempting a mixed-instance deploy: create 8x small-gpu nodes instead of 2x large-gpu. Kicking off a create: 
```bash
aws-cli ec2 request-instances --count 8 --instance-type g4dn.xlarge --region us-west-2 --ami ami-inference-2026
```

infra-bot: ACTION LOGGED: incident.assign -> sre-oncall; incident.sev -> high; incident-channel -> this thread.

kyra: small-instance creation in progress. If those land we can evict lower-priority jobs to make room for online inference.

~9 minutes later~

kyra: 6/8 small instances are up and joined the cluster. Early capacity relief observed. Queue now 900. p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 ~ 4.2s.

jordan.t: great improvement. We still have a tail—recommend we keep fallback routing for another hour and then remove if stable. Also consider a short-lived feature flag to drop heavy batched requests.

maria.k: I'll coordinate with product to toggle the batched upstream flag. Also capturing repro prompts to add to Optimize recommendations.

sre-oncall: on-call Handoff: handing to kyra for night shift monitoring. Key notes in runbook: quota ticket #78910 pending, fallback routing enabled, token-size throttle enabled, mixed-instance small-GPU pool created. If queue >1500 re-open pager.

kyra: ack — I'll monitor dashboards and push updates. Assigning follow-ups: 
- infra: follow up with cloud quota team for permanent quota increase (owner: kyra)
- eng: evaluate autoscaler retry/backoff to avoid thundering retries (owner: jordan.t)
- product: notify affected enterprise CSMs if any customers request escalation (owner: maria.k)

support-bot: Customer update draft: "We experienced an increase in hosted API latency due to a rapid traffic spike that temporarily exhausted available GPU capacity in us-west-2. We routed lower-tier traffic to a fallback model to preserve latency for enterprise customers and are provisioning additional capacity. If you are seeing degraded quality, please reply and include request IDs."

eng-lead: good work. Postmortem: schedule for tomorrow 11:00 PT. Capture root cause: over-aggressive scheduling change in provisioner + insufficient quota for peak scaling. Also document fallback routing as part of default playbook.

sre-oncall: incident closed (status: degraded->recovering). Final metrics snapshot: peak queue 4200, time to first mitigation 6m, time to stable p95 <1.5s = 28m.

kyra: leaving final note: next steps — tighten autoscaler backoff, add pre-warm hooks for predicted traffic bursts, and add an alert for cloud quota errors (special-case 429).
